title: Dem senator turns ‘leader of the free world’ title on its head with Zelenskyy remarks
summary: Chris Coons declared Volodymyr Zelenskyy is now the free world's primary leader, igniting fierce backlash from the White House and conservatives.
story: Fox News correspondent Stephanie Bennett reports from London as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meets with European allies in Belgrade and pushes for additional air-defense aid amid continued pressure on Russia. The talks come as the U.S. Senate passes a sweeping sanctions bill targeting Moscow.

Delaware Sen. Chris Coons is facing backlash after declaring that the United States is "no longer" the leader of the free world and pointing instead to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as the national leader putting his country "on the line for freedom."

"I would say we are no longer the leaders of the free world. In fact, if anything, Volodymyr Zelenskyy is the primary national leader who is putting his country’s men and women on the line for freedom," Coons said during a town hall earlier this month.
"We need to earn our place back as leader in the free world in the future."

Coons’ remarks underscore his long-running alignment with Kyiv at a moment when President Donald Trump is pressing for an end to the war and putting a renewed emphasis on American power and national pride.
TRUMP HAILS AMERICA AS 'MOST EXCEPTIONAL NATION EVER TO EXIST' IN MOUNT RUSHMORE SPEECH

The Delaware Democrat has been one of Congress’ more outspoken supporters of Ukraine, repeatedly backing military aid, tougher sanctions on Russia and continued U.S. engagement with Zelenskyy’s government.
President Donald Trump greets Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House Aug. 18, 2025 in Washington, D.C.  (Getty Images)
Coons spoke with Dover, Delaware, Councilman Andre Boggerty alongside Rep. Sarah McBride in a virtual town hall Tuesday hosted by the Kent County Democratic Committee focused on local issues.

Coons has been a vocal advocate for sustained U.S. support for Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, repeatedly pressing for military assistance and tougher sanctions on Moscow. Coons visited Kyiv in 2022 to meet with Zelenskyy and visited Odesa with Senate Foreign Relations Committee members in February to reiterate "the ironclad, bipartisan support" for Ukraine, according to a press release.
Nick Adams, special presidential envoy for American tourism, exceptionalism and values, told Fox News Digital Coons' comments are "the essence of America last."

"The United States is today, has been since 1776, and with God's grace, always will be the leader of the free world. To suggest otherwise is to ignore our Constitution and the bloodshed by our heroes who made sure that our Declaration of Independence would not just be a theoretical document but the beginning of a new era in the history of humanity," Adams said.
Adams added that no other nation can hold a candle to America, pointing to its constitutional freedoms, founding principles of liberty and belief that natural rights transcend government authority.
WORLD LEADERS, DIGNITARIES PAY TRIBUTE TO AMERICA ON HISTORIC 250TH BIRTHDAY

Chris Coons attends a press conference with an American delegation, consisting of senators and members of the House of Representatives, in Copenhagen, Denmark, Jan. 17, 2026. (Ida Marie Odgaard/Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Images)

"To say otherwise is to reveal an unbelievable ignorance as to what our nation is, where we came from and how our destiny will always be shaped by the principles of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness," Adams added.
Conservative critics seized on Coons' remarks, accusing him of being "anti-American."

"Wow! This is truly sick behavior. Sen. Chris Coons — a Democrat who nobody has ever heard of, but nonetheless a U.S. Senator — says the U.S. is ‘no longer the leaders of the free world’ because ‘Volodymyr Zelenskyy is the primary national leader,’" the White House’s Rapid Response account wrote on X.
"Imagine asserting this. What an absolute clown," one user wrote.
"Chris Coons has always been an anti-American fraud. He’s a total coward," another person said.
ZELENSKYY PRESSURES US AND EUROPE FOR MORE 'AIR DEFENSE' ASSISTANCE AMID ONGOING WAR WITH RUSSIA
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meets with President Donald Trump at the White House during his visit to Washington, D.C., July 28. (Zelenskyy Social Media Account/Anadolu via Getty Images)
"What an embarrassment he is — Ukraine hasn’t held elections since 2019," a user commented.
The Russia-Ukraine war has dragged on for more than four years, with Kyiv holding off a larger Russian force while facing manpower shortages and relying heavily on continued Western weapons.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Zelenskyy met with Trump in the Oval Office July 28, and the two discussed licensing Ukraine to produce Patriot missile interceptors as Kyiv seeks to strengthen its air defenses.
Coons' office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's press inquiry.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

title: Democrats condemning Hasan Piker as backlash spreads through party
summary: Hakeem Jeffries called Hasan Piker's remarks about American Jews "dangerous and antisemitic" as top Democrats lined up to condemn the streamer.
story: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed faces scrutiny over his campaign's ties to far-left streamer Hasan Piker. Piker's highly controversial remarks about U.S. Jews prompt prominent Democrats to warn colleagues to distance themselves.
Prominent Democrats are lining up to condemn far-left streamer Hasan Piker after he warned that American Jews could face violence if they continue to be seen as strongly supporting Israel.
The backlash follows a stream last week in which Piker displayed an image of Michigan state Sen. Jeremy Moss, who is Jewish and the Democratic nominee in Michigan's 11th Congressional District.
Moss has said a fake audio clip is being circulated that falsely portrays him as saying he ran for Congress solely to ensure continued U.S. support for Israel.

"If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said.
PIKER DEMANDS DEMOCRATS DEFEND HIM FROM ATTACKS, CLAIMS HE’S NO ‘TOXIC RADICAL FORCE'

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is facing renewed scrutiny after viewers spotted a framed newspaper front page from Sept. 12, 2001, in his background. (Sam Barnes/Web Summit via Sportsfile via Getty Images)

Piker's comments drew criticism from top Democrats, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and DNC Chair Ken Martin, as well as lawmakers who have criticized him before. Others who have appeared with Piker or defended engaging with him are now pushing back on his remarks.
Here are the Democrats speaking out:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y.

Jeffries joined the backlash Monday, initially without mentioning Piker by name. The House Democratic leader called the claim that American Jews were inviting violence against themselves "dangerous and antisemitic."
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., spoke during a news conference at the U.S. Capitol July 13, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)
Asked on CNN the following day whether he was referring to Piker, Jeffries said yes.
"Those comments were dangerous, malicious and antisemitic and should not be tolerated by anyone in the public square," Jeffries said.
Rep. Brad Schneider, D-Ill.

Schneider was one of the first Democratic lawmakers to publicly take on Piker, calling him an "unapologetic antisemite" in March and warning fellow Democrats against giving a platform to people who espouse hate.
PIKER DEMANDS DEMOCRATS DEFEND HIM FROM ATTACKS, CLAIMS HE’S NO ‘TOXIC RADICAL FORCE'
Schneider renewed that criticism Tuesday, saying Piker's latest remarks were consistent with his "history of antisemitic statements."
"Hasan Piker's hateful ideas and antisemitic remarks have no place in America or our nation's politics," Schneider said.
Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich.
Slotkin, who had previously criticized Piker and his involvement in Michigan Democratic politics, spoke out again after his latest comments.
Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., walks into the Senate Chamber in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images, File)
"No community should face the threat [of] violence for their political views," Slotkin said, rejecting the idea that Jewish Americans should be blamed for antisemitism directed at them.
Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich.
Stevens criticized Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed earlier this year for campaigning with Piker and made clear she would not do the same.
Piker was the "exact opposite" of someone she would campaign with, Stevens said. She later said she believed Piker should be condemned.
Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J.
Booker's team had already kept its distance from Piker, turning down an appearance with the streamer over his past comments.

Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., speaks alongside Democratic Senate Judiciary Committee members during a news conference on the nomination of acting Attorney General Todd Blanche on Capitol Hill July 15, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Eric Lee/Getty Images)
Booker went further this week, directly condemning Piker's rhetoric about Jewish Americans and saying it has no place in public discourse.
Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow
In April, McMorrow criticized Piker's role in Michigan Democratic politics and his inflammatory style.
She compared Piker's approach to that of far-right commentator Nick Fuentes, arguing that both use inflammatory rhetoric to attract attention.
Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J.

Gottheimer has been among Piker's most persistent Democratic critics. In April, he joined Republican Rep. Mike Lawler of New York in introducing a bipartisan House resolution condemning antisemitic rhetoric from Piker and Candace Owens.

Rep. Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., listens during a news conference on new legislation to support Holocaust education nationwide at the U.S. Capitol Jan. 27, 2023, in Washington, D.C. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

In an interview on Fox News' "America's Newsroom," Gottheimer praised Jeffries pushback against Piker, calling the streamer’s comments something "right out of the Nazi playbook," emphasizing them as "a call for violence against Jews."
Gottheimer on Tuesday also called on House leaders to bring the resolution up for a vote.
He also told CNN in an interview that anyone who does not condemn Piker’s comments is "complicit."
HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED'
James Carville
Longtime Democratic strategist James Carville drew a line between himself and part of the Democratic Party embracing Piker earlier this month.
Carville said he would leave the party if Piker's wing took control, arguing there was no room for both of them under the same political tent.
James Carville speaks onstage during the Carville: Winning is Everything, Stupid! Q&A at the 27th SCAD Savannah Film Festival in Savannah, Ga., on Oct. 31, 2024. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images for SCAD)

He later told Fox News' "Jesse Watters Primetime" he is not concerned about socialists taking over the Democratic Party, dismissing the party's socialist flank as a "pack of fools" and "a bunch of silly people."
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa.
Fetterman earlier this month took aim at El-Sayed over his ties to Piker during Michigan's Democratic Senate primary.
"I dare you to continue to campaign with people like Hasan Piker," Fetterman said.
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., speaks to members of the media in the Senate Subway of the U.s. Capitol in Washington, D.C., June 2, 2026. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Fetterman's comments were aimed primarily at Democrats associating with Piker rather than a direct response to the streamer's latest remarks.
Rep. Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla.
Moskowitz distanced himself from Piker last week after defeating a Democratic primary challenger who had Piker's backing.
The Florida Democrat made clear after the race that he wanted no association with Piker or his politics.
Rep. Jake Auchincloss, D-Mass.
Auchincloss rejected Piker's politics during an appearance on "Fox News Sunday," drawing a clear distinction between the streamer and the Democratic Party.
"The Democratic Party does not stand for what Hasan Piker stands for," Auchincloss said.
HASAN PIKER STANDS BY 'INTENTIONALLY PROVOCATIVE' CLAIMS THAT HAMAS IS 'A THOUSAND TIMES BETTER' THAN ISRAEL
Rep. Hillary Scholten, D-Mich.
Scholten issued one of the sharpest responses after Piker's comments about American Jews and Michigan state Sen. Jeremy Moss.
"Hasan Piker's talk of violence against American Jews and directly naming a Michigan elected official and future member of Congress, Jeremy Moss, is unacceptable. Full stop," Scholten said Monday.
She also called Piker a "hack who thrives on hate, shock and awe" and said his rhetoric had no place in Michigan or the country.
Michigan state Sen. Jeremy Moss, D
Moss, who was directly discussed during Piker's stream, on Monday pushed back after Piker displayed his image while talking about American Jews and Israel.
Moss said there was "no room for extremism in Michigan."
Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif.
Khanna's response was notable because he has appeared on Piker's show and previously defended his decision to engage with the streamer.

But on Monday, Khanna rejected Piker's latest argument, saying antisemitism should be condemned unequivocally and that Jewish people and supporters of Israel are not responsible for antisemitism directed at them.
Abdul El-Sayed
El-Sayed, whose Michigan Senate campaign has faced criticism over his association with Piker, sought to put some distance between his campaign and the streamer after the latest controversy on Monday.
Twitch streamer Hasan Piker appeared on the campaign trail with Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)
El-Sayed said Piker does not speak for him or his campaign and condemned antisemitism. He stopped short, however, of directly condemning Piker himself.
DEMOCRATIC MICHIGAN AG ACCUSES HER PARTY OF 'ABSOLUTELY NOT' DOING ENOUGH TO COUNTER ANTISEMITISM
DNC Chair Ken Martin
Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin joined the criticism Tuesday, bringing the national party's leadership into the dispute.
Martin condemned the idea that American Jews should be blamed for hatred, threats or violence directed at them, calling such rhetoric dangerous, wrong and antisemitic.
Sen. Jacky Rosen, D-Nev.
Rosen, co-chair of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, said Piker had used antisemitic tropes before but on Tuesday described his latest remarks as "a new low."
The Nevada Democrat rejected the suggestion that Jewish Americans bear responsibility for antisemitism or violence directed at them.
Rep. Ritchie Torres, D-N.Y.
Torres, a longtime Piker critic, again spoke out Tuesday after the streamer's comments about American Jews.
The New York Democrat accused Piker of blaming Jewish victims for the antisemitism directed against them, adding to his previous criticism of the streamer.
Rep. Greg Stanton, D-Ariz.
Stanton joined the Democrats speaking out Tuesday over Piker's latest comments.
The Arizona congressman rejected the argument that Jewish Americans bear responsibility for hatred or violence directed against them.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Fox News Digital's Paul Steinhauser and Elizabeth Elkind contributed to this report.

title: Millions of barrels of Iranian oil sit beyond Trump blockade as he vows ‘zero leakage’
summary: Nearly 40 million barrels of Iranian crude sit on tankers near Malaysia, posing a test for Trump's "zero-leakage" sanctions campaign against Tehran.
story: Fox Business correspondent Lauren Simonetti reveals Iran's critical oil situation, highlighting why seizing Kharg Island is considered a 'nuclear option.' Simonetti presents data showing Iran's oil storage tanks are 77% full, with 46 Iranian oil ships caught in a US blockade. She details Iran's ship-to-ship transfer tactics to circumvent sanctions.
Far from the U.S. warships enforcing a blockade at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, nearly 40 million barrels of Iranian crude are sitting aboard tankers in waters near Malaysia, east of Singapore.

The cargo amounts to roughly 20 very large crude carriers’ worth of oil, a floating stockpile that could still give Tehran a way to turn crude already outside the blockade zone into cash even as the blockade sharply restricts fresh exports.
The stockpile poses a test for the Trump administration as it moves from military action and a naval blockade toward what the White House calls its financial "endgame" against Tehran.
TRUMP’S IRAN CRACKDOWN ‘SUFFOCATING’ REGIME AS OIL WELLS COULD SHUT WITHIN DAYS, BESSENT SAYS
Oil tankers and cargo ships line up in the Strait of Hormuz as seen from Khor Fakkan, United Arab Emirates, March 11, 2026. (AP Photo/Altaf Qadri)

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday launched Operation Economic Outcast, promising a "zero-leakage approach" designed to cut off Iran's remaining sources of revenue after months of pressure on its oil sales, shipping networks and financial enablers.

The blockade appears to be making it substantially harder for Iran to export new oil. China’s imports of Iranian crude have fallen to an estimated 534,000 barrels per day so far this month, down from roughly 823,000 barrels per day in July, according to provisional Kpler data reported by Reuters.

But millions of barrels that moved beyond the blockade line before it tightened remain within potential reach of buyers. Iran has an estimated 80 million barrels of crude held in floating storage, Reuters reported, with roughly half aboard vessels near Malaysia.
That leaves Washington facing a different challenge: stopping Tehran from monetizing oil the blockade did not trap.
If Iran can still turn that crude into cash, the regime can use the proceeds to pay for imports and potentially finance efforts to rebuild its military even as the blockade restricts fresh exports.
That makes the tankers near Malaysia an early test of whether the administration can deliver the "total isolation" it has promised.
CHINA ORDERS FIRMS TO IGNORE US IRAN SANCTIONS, DARING US TO ENFORCE CRACKDOWN

"The blockade as it’s currently being practiced and enforced against isn’t really stopping the flow of Iranian oil that’s already past the blockade line," Max Meizlish, a former Treasury official focused on sanctions policy and current senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital.
Secretary Scott Bessent speaks at a news conference, Monday, Aug. 24, 2026, at the Treasury Department in Washington. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

Iranian oil can move through ship-to-ship transfers, in which cargo is shifted from one tanker to another at sea. The practice can help obscure the oil’s origin before it reaches a buyer, often an independent Chinese refinery.

Simply having the crude outside the blockade zone does not automatically give Tehran usable revenue. Iran still needs to deliver the oil, collect payment and move the proceeds through the financial channels it has used to evade sanctions.

Treasury has said Iran primarily settles oil sales in Chinese yuan, with exchange houses and front companies helping convert those funds into currencies the regime can use. The department has also previously tied proceeds from Iranian oil sales to the Iranian government, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, weapons development and Tehran’s regional proxies.

Meizlish noted that the administration has continued sanctioning Chinese and Hong Kong trading houses, maritime service providers and other entities accused of enabling Iranian sanctions evasion but has stopped short of designating a Chinese financial institution.

The U.S. cut the bank off from access to the American financial system in 2012 over dealings with Iran, Meizlish said, but stopped short of placing it on Treasury’s Specially Designated Nationals list. He argued that formally designating the bank could put pressure on its owner, China National Petroleum Corporation, and potentially disrupt a channel used to move Iranian oil revenue.
A ship passes through the Strait of Hormuz during a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran on April 8, 2026. (Shady Alassar/Anadolu/Getty Images)

Meizlish noted that the administration has continued sanctioning Chinese and Hong Kong trading houses, maritime service providers and other entities accused of enabling Iranian sanctions evasion, but has so far stopped short of designating a Chinese financial institution.
"Secretary Bessent didn’t mention China by name," he said, adding that the issue could become a subject of higher-level engagement between Washington and Beijing.
The administration has already targeted the Malaysia route.
In April, Treasury sanctioned the Hong Kong-flagged tanker Lynn, saying the vessel conducted a ship-to-ship transfer of Iranian crude off Malaysia before delivering the cargo to China.
Meizlish said another option would be to expand pressure on shadow-fleet vessels operating near Malaysia and elsewhere in Asia in an effort to keep that oil from ultimately reaching Chinese buyers.

"The U.S. could expand the blockades in that sense by going after shadow fleet tankers, operating, for instance, off the coast of Malaysia, which is a huge hub for illicit ship-to-ship transfers," he said.

He said the sharp decline in Chinese purchases suggests the pressure campaign is having an effect, but argued that crude already aboard shadow-fleet tankers remains a potential future source of revenue for Tehran.
"There’s a lot more that we can do," Meizlish said.

"Unless we expect for this regime to ultimately fall, we should be putting a lot of pressure into interdicting this oil that’s on the market right now on shadow fleet tankers, because this money could eventually go into the regime’s pockets down the road," he said.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Asked whether the administration planned further action against Iranian oil cargoes and shadow-fleet vessels near Malaysia, a War Department official told Fox News Digital that U.S. forces would continue "global maritime enforcement" to disrupt illicit networks and interdict sanctioned vessels supporting Iran "wherever they operate, at the time and place of our choosing."

"Under Operation Economic Outcast, anyone foolish enough to continue doing business with the Iranian regime cannot continue to enjoy access to the global financial system," a Treasury Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "We will cut every remaining economic lifeline Tehran has."
Meizlish said money from oil already sitting on shadow-fleet tankers could still wind up in Tehran’s hands and help Iran rebuild military capabilities damaged in the conflict.

Going after those tankers would not be simple. The U.S. Navy is already stretched by operations in the Strait of Hormuz and elsewhere, he said, and seizing ships and their cargo can trigger legal fights over ownership, custody and what happens to the oil afterward.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Meizlish said Congress could make it easier for the government to seize illicit cargoes. He also argued that Washington should look for ways to expand its capacity to pursue shadow-fleet vessels if the Navy cannot do it alone.

Bessent’s new campaign goes beyond oil, targeting digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. He also threatened broader secondary sanctions against entities that continue doing business with Tehran.
The drop in Chinese purchases shows Iran is having a harder time getting new oil to market. But millions of barrels are already sitting outside the blockade.
Whether Tehran can still sell that oil, and whether Washington is willing to go after it near Malaysia, will help determine how much "zero leakage" actually means.

title: CIA Director John Ratcliffe met with Russian intelligence officials in visit to Moscow, Kremlin says
summary: Video captured a C-17 Globemaster landing at Moscow's Vnukovo airport as CIA Director John Ratcliffe reportedly met with Russian intelligence officials.
story: A video captured a U.S. military C-17A Globemaster III aircraft coming in for a landing on Wednesday, Aug. 25, 2026, at Moscow's Vnukovo airport. (Credit: Reuters)

CIA Director John Ratcliffe flew to Moscow to meet with Russian intelligence officials, the Kremlin reportedly said Wednesday, after video emerged of a U.S. military transport plane coming in for a landing Tuesday at Vnukovo airport.
President Donald Trump, when asked this morning about Ratcliffe’s visit on "The Glenn Beck Program," said, "He’s there on, you know, very sort of semi-routine."
"We would like to see the war with Ukraine end," Trump added, before saying, "Now something may come out of it.
"We're working very hard to get that war ended and frankly they both want to see it ended at this point."
Fox News Digital has reached out to the White House, the CIA and the U.S. Embassy in Moscow for further comment.
US MILITARY PLANE LANDS IN MOSCOW, WITH KREMLIN CLAIMING IT HAS NO INFORMATION: REPORT
President Donald Trump shakes hands with CIA Director John Ratcliffe during a press conference at the White House in Washington, D.C., on April 6, 2026. (Reuters)

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Wednesday, according to Reuters, "All I can ⁠tell you is that there have been contacts via the security services. I can tell you that there have been no meetings with the Russian president."
The news agency cited the Kremlin as saying Ratcliffe met with Russian intelligence officials.
"Naturally, President Putin is kept informed of everything without delay," Peskov also was quoted as saying.
The last CIA director to visit Moscow was William Burns in November 2021, three months before Russia’s war against Ukraine started, Reuters reported.
A senior Ukrainian official told The Associated Press that Washington informed Kyiv a delegation would be traveling to the Russian capital and asked it to suspend strikes until it left.
PUTIN 'PANICKED' AS DEFIANT UKRAINE MARKS INDEPENDENCE DAY UNDER RUSSIAN BOMBARDMENT
A U.S. military transport plane approaches Moscow, Russia, on Wednesday, Aug. 25, 2026, in this screen grab taken from a social media video. (Reuters)

The official said the request did not apply to all Russian territory, but specifically to Moscow, St. Petersburg and some northern regions. Strikes on other parts of Russia continued, the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because he is not authorized to talk publicly.
Video captured a U.S. military transport plane coming in for a landing Tuesday at Moscow's Vnukovo airport, in a flight that the Kremlin initially claimed it had no information about.

Data from the website Flightradar24 showed that the Boeing C-17A Globemaster III left Joint Base Andrews in Maryland early Sunday afternoon on a flight to Riga, Latvia. The aircraft then traveled from Riga to Moscow on Tuesday morning.
President Donald Trump and John Ratcliffe, CIA director, speak as they leave a Cabinet meeting at Camp David in Thurmont, Md., on July 31, 2026. (Reuters)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The last time a U.S.-registered jet made a direct flight to Russia from Europe was in January when special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, visited Moscow for a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin about the war in Ukraine, according to Reuters.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Democratic officials charged for allegedly scamming COVID relief funds
summary: Two Democratic Party officials in Massachusetts face federal indictments alleging they schemed to steal over $700,000 in COVID relief funds.
story: Officials in Massachusetts arrested State Rep. Francisco Paulino for allegedly stealing pandemic relief money. He's the second state politician charged this month.
Authorities arrested a Democratic Party official for alleged COVID fraud for the second time this month on Wednesday.

U.S. Attorney Leah Foley says police arrested Massachusetts state Rep. Francisco Paulino early Wednesday morning, charging him with 11 counts related to pandemic unemployment insurance fraud, pandemic loan fraud and money laundering.

"According to the Paulino indictment, Mr. Paulino devised a scheme to obtain more than $700,000 in federal pandemic relief funds. It is alleged that Paulino used some of the money for his own personal use, including real estate expenses, loan payments and transfers to his campaign account," Foley said.
"Other money he flipped around and lent to other individuals at higher interest rates than the pandemic loan rate," she continued.
11 SUSPECTED ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS AMONG 15 ARRESTED IN $1.4M BENEFITS FRAUD CRACKDOWN IN MASSACHUSETTS, DOJ SAYS
Rep. Francisco E. Paulino watches as Gov. Maura Healey signs healthcare legislation on Jan. 8. (Stuart Cahill/Boston Herald)
The indictment says Paulino's alleged fraud began in 2020 when he signed up for COVID relief funding on behalf of "an unwitting 77-year-old relative."

Paulino's arrest comes roughly a week after the FBI arrested Lawrence Mayor Brian DePeña on similar charges. A federal grand jury also handed down an 11-count indictment against DePeña with charges relating to pandemic loan fraud and money laundering.
The FBI says DePeña first began "diverting public funds" in 2020 when he was serving on the Lawrence city council. He was arrested earlier this month.
MINNESOTA FRAUD MASTERMIND GETS NEARLY 42 YEARS IN PRISON IN MASSIVE $250M 'FEEDING OUR FUTURE' SCHEME

Lawrence Mayor Brian DePena faces federal charges for allegedly using pandemic-relief funds for his mayoral campaign and to pay off his personal debts. DePena applied for the funds to help Tenares Tire Services Inc., his tire shop in Lawrence, federal prosecutors said. (City of Lawrence)

"Everyone listening today knows how difficult it was for Americans during the pandemic," Foley said. "The money these two individuals allegedly scammed was meant for hardworking Americans and struggling business owners, not for two greedy individuals who lied and stole for their own personal benefit."
The FBI logo is seen at the Los Angeles Federal Building on June 4, 2025, in Los Angeles. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

"It is never a proud moment when we arrest a public official, but we will continue to do it until the message is received: No one is above the law, and no one gets a pass," she added.
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: Trump scores federal court win against House progressive accused of assaulting ICE
summary: A Biden-appointed judge sided with Trump's DOJ, rejecting House Democrat LaMonica McIver's legislative immunity argument for getting her case thrown out.
story: Lawmakers clash at a House Judiciary Committee hearing over immigration enforcement and conditions at New Jersey's Delaney Hall Detention Center. Bill Melugin reports as Republicans reject what they call ‘false narratives’ about ICE's treatment of detainees, while Democrats point to alleged inhumane conditions and hunger strikes at the facility on ‘Special Report.’

A federal judge appointed by former President Joe Biden is siding with the Trump administration in refusing to dismiss a case against a House Democrat accused of assaulting federal immigration officers.

Two of the three judges on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit refused to dismiss the Department of Justice (DOJ) case against Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., stemming from a 2025 incident at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Newark, New Jersey.

An unannounced visit to the Delaney Hall detention center by a group of Democratic officials devolved into chaos in May 2025 that culminated in a physical standoff between federal lawmakers and ICE agents and the arrest of Newark Mayor Ras Baraka. McIver was charged with three counts, including assaulting and impeding federal officers.
FIVE ANTI-ICE AGITATORS ARRESTED DURING CHAOTIC DELANEY HALL CONFRONTATIONS CAUGHT ON VIDEO
President Donald Trump listens as administration officials speak during an event in the Oval Office of the White House on Oct. 16, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
She attempted to get the case thrown out, arguing that she is immune from prosecution because her actions were part of her official duties as a member of Congress.
She also accused the DOJ of unfairly singling her out, with her congressional office calling the charges "vindictive."
DOJ VOWS TO APPEAL AFTER JUDGE DISMISSES SMUGGLING CHARGES AGAINST KILMAR ABREGO GARCIA AS 'VINDICTIVE'

But the 2-1 decision, made by Biden-appointed Judge Cindy Chung and Trump-appointed Judge Stephanos Bibas, stated that McIver's argument of legislative immunity would not stand for two of the three counts, while the third count was sent back to a lower court for further review.
Rep. LaMonica McIver, D-N.J., demands the release of Newark Mayor Ras Baraka after his arrest while protesting outside an ICE facility on May 9, 2025, in Newark, N.J. (Angelina Katsanis/AP)

Court documents say McIver allegedly "slammed her forearm" into a federal officer trying to arrest Baraka. On that count, the federal appellate court agreed with a lower court decision that her "alleged intervention into the Mayor’s questionable arrest had no cognizable connection to any legislative function" protected by the Constitution.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT
The second count alleged that McIver used both of her forearms to "strike [an officer] as she returned inside of the secured area of Delaney Hall."
The two judges wrote, "Like the acts charged in Count One, the acts of pushing past and forcibly striking someone are unambiguously non-legislative: they are not integral to the legislative process."
Protesters gather outside the federal immigration center at Delaney Hall, where ICE is housing detained illegal immigrants, on June 3, 2026, in Newark, New Jersey. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
Judge Thomas Ambro wrote in dissent, "When an Executive Branch official prevents a Member from entering a DHS facility, she is denied effective access to an oversight inspection."
McIver herself said in a statement that "the court got it wrong."

"Today’s decision chills that authority and emboldens the Trump administration to continue persecuting our most vulnerable communities, those who try to defend them, and anyone who dares hold the president or his lackeys accountable. I will not fold to this administration. We are exploring every possible option. The administration will not stop me from doing my job or standing for what is right. This is not over," McIver said.

title: Philadelphia DA says he'll keep piece of Trump's White House ballroom 'after we all blow it up'
summary: Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said Tuesday he expects President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom to one day be blown up in an “official ceremony."
story: Chanley Painter reports on the legal battle surrounding White House ballroom construction after an appeals court blocked the project. Former administration official Stephen Miller argues the facility is a national security necessity.
Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said Tuesday he was going to keep a piece of President Donald Trump's White House ballroom as a paperweight "after we all blow it up."

"In about 10 to 15 years, we are all going to be sitting here with smiles on our faces," Krasner said, according to video footage obtained by WCAU. "And I'm going to have a paperweight sitting on my desk. And do you know what that paper weight's going to be? It's going to be a piece of the ballroom after we blow it up."

Krasner, who has previously called Trump a fascist and said he would hunt down Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers, made the comments while speaking at George Washington's historic home in Philadelphia during the city's annual slavery commiseration, according to WCAU.
DEM JUSTICES SLAP SOROS-BACKED PHILLY DA WITH POWER STRIP IN STUNNING DECISION: 'NOT RELIABLE'
Krasner first called Trump "a pain in the a--," to which an audience member responded, "No, he's the devil!"
Krasner then responded, "He's the devil, all right, well there is some evidence to that effect."
District Attorney Larry Krasner is seen leaving Fox 29's "Good Day" at FOX 29 Studios on Aug. 24, 2023, in Philadelphia. (Gilbert Carrasquillo/GC Images)
"The man himself is the embodiment of hate. He is the embodiment of ignorance. He is the embodiment of depriving people of their vote and their education. That's who he is," Krasner continued.
TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY
Krasner was specifically bashing Trump for deciding to replace a slavery exhibit at the Washington home under a March executive order titled, "Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History."

Under the order, the National Park Service replaced the panels dedicated to showcasing the history of George Washington's slaves with more broad displays of U.S. history. A protracted legal battle between the city and the Trump administration most recently saw a federal appeals court side with the federal government and rule that Philadelphia had no legal right to dictate the content of the displays at the federally owned site.
JUDGE BLOCKS PHILADELPHIA LAW TARGETING MASKED FEDERAL OFFICERS
A National Parks Service police officer looks at the displays installed by the Trump administration at the President's House in Philadelphia. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)
Despite the city's loss to the federal government in the legal fight, Krasner remained defiant.

"This memorial will be here, the educational content will be here," Krasner railed Tuesday. "People will be coming to see it, not for a year or two, or not even 20 years. They will be coming to see it as long as this federal park is here."
EXCLUSIVE: KENNEDY CENTER BOARD MOVES TO NAME GROUNDS ‘PRESIDENT DONALD J TRUMP PLAZA'
"But let me tell you what will not be here," he continued.
"There will not be a ballroom. There will not be a Kennedy Center renamed for a fool," Krasner said.
Larry Krasner departs after a hearing at City Hall in Philadelphia on Oct. 31, 2024. (Ryan Collerd/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Krasner did specify that the envisioned demolition would be "in an official ceremony, just to be clear, in an official ceremony we're gonna blow it up and we're gonna give the taxpayers their money back by selling old pieces as paperweights, and I'm gonna have one on my desk."
WHITE HOUSE SEIZES ON DELAYED OBAMA PRESIDENTIAL CENTER OPENING TO CROWN TRUMP ‘BUILDER-IN-CHIEF’
The White House fired back at Krasner's comments about the ballroom project.

"President Trump continues to implement long-overdue and necessary renovations to beautify the People’s House as we approach our great Nation’s 250th anniversary of independence. Thanks to the Builder-in-Chief, the White House will be properly glorified and remain in excellent condition for generations to come. Only people who suffer from a severe and incurable disease known as Trump Derangement Syndrome would find a problem with that," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

When reached by Fox News Digital, Nate Herring, the U.S. Secret Service's lead public affairs specialist, said, "The U.S. Secret Service investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees. Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence."

title: Maverick Democrat surges with Republicans as his own party turns on him, stoking talk of GOP switch
summary: John Fetterman now holds a 73% favorability among Pennsylvania Republicans, surpassing Dave McCormick's 63%, as party switch speculation grows.
story: Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., assesses how the Democratic Party is responding to the rise of socialist, far-left candidates on ‘Hannity.’

Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, a centrist Democrat known for bashing his party's left flank, is more popular among Keystone State Republicans than their own GOP senator, Sen. Dave McCormick, according to a new poll.

The release of the poll this week by the New York Times, Philadelphia Inquirer and Siena University is further evidence that Fetterman, who at times breaks with his party and aligns with President Donald Trump, and who is a frequent guest on the Fox News Channel, has become increasingly popular among Republicans.
The survey may boost speculation that the first-term senator could potentially bolt the Democrats and become a Republican. But Fetterman has denied that he plans to leave the Democratic Party.

Nearly 3 in 4 Republican registered voters in Pennsylvania (73%) held a favorable opinion of Fetterman, according to the poll. That's 10 points higher than the 63% of Republicans in the state who viewed McCormick favorably.
DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB
Sen. John Fetterman speaks to members of the media in the Senate Subway of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C., on June 2, 2026. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The 73% of Republicans who view Fetterman favorably is a major increase from the 25% who said the same thing in 2024, two years after the senator was elected.
But Fetterman's standing among Democrats continued to sink, according to the poll.

Just 22% of registered Democrats in Pennsylvania said they had a favorable view of Fetterman, while 63% viewed him unfavorably. That's a dramatic reversal from two years ago, when 74% of Democrats viewed Fetterman favorably.
The survey also indicated that by a 49%-35% margin, independents held a favorable view of Fetterman.

Matt Beynon, a veteran Pennsylvania-based Republican consultant, told Fox News Digital, "I think a lot of Republicans appreciate the fact that Sen. Fetterman is willing to stick his thumb in the radical wing of his party’s eye on issues like antisemitism."
WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS IN THE MIDTERM RACES SHOW
Fetterman's growing popularity among Republicans has fueled speculation that he leave the Democratic Party before potentially facing a primary challenge when he's up for re-election in 2028.

The senator, who is a strong supporter of Israel, has increasingly railed against fellow Democrats who have criticized Israeli leaders over their ongoing war against Hamas in Gaza. Fetterman has said he has "no plans" to leave the Democratic Party. But he added if Democrats officially became the "anti-Israel party," count him out.

"My long-term concern has been with the Democratic Party, as I am a member of that, is that our party is going to back away and turn their back to Israel," he said last month at a Hill Nation Summit in Washington, D.C.
"If our party ever becomes, and just makes it official, the anti-Israel party, that’s when I would leave because that’s been a moral clarity for me."
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Sen. John Fetterman participated in a forum moderated by Fox News’ Shannon Bream alongside his Republican counterpart, Sen. Dave McCormick. (Fox Nation)
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other Senate Republicans have reached out to Fetterman regarding a party switch.

"I have had conversations with him in the past, as have many of my colleagues about the challenges he faces in his caucus. And there are many of us who, I think, would welcome the opportunity to have him join the Republican conference, but ultimately that’s a decision that’s up to him," Thune told reporters in July.

But Beynon said that regardless of Fetterman's growing popularity among Republicans, "when it comes time for the senator’s re-election campaign in 2028, those same voters will be reminded that John Fetterman votes with Democrats more than 90% of the time."
Fox News Digital reached out to the senator's office for comment regarding the new poll, but did not receive a response at the time this story was published.

title: Green New Dodge: El-Sayed runs from policy as newly surfaced deleted posts show years of support
summary: Abdul El-Sayed refused to defend the Green New Deal on air, but deleted posts show he once wrote "I believe in a Green New Deal" in all caps.
story: Fox News host Jesse Watters spoke to Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed about Green New Deal policies on 'Jesse Watters Primetime.'

Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed told Fox News host Jesse Watters on Monday that he would not defend the Green New Deal when confronted with his past support for the progressive climate proposal, a notable shift from years of publicly embracing it by name.

"Look, I’m not going to defend the Green New Deal," El-Sayed told Watters after the host confronted him over his past support for the proposal. When Watters reiterated that El-Sayed was on record supporting it, El-Sayed redirected the discussion toward lowering energy costs and creating Michigan jobs by prioritizing renewables.

Michigan, which Trump won in 2024 but lost in 2020, is shaping up to have one of the most competitive Senate races in the country, with the likely narrow results in the state potentially determining control of Congress. Critics charge that El-Sayed is downplaying some of his past beliefs and scrubbing his online footprint to appear more moderate, and therefore more palatable, to Michigan voters.
UNEARTHED CLIP EXPOSES MORE ANTI-POLICE RHETORIC AS EL-SAYED GETS GRILLED FOR DELETING SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS
Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed at a campaign event in Detroit, Michigan, on Aug. 2, 2026. ( )
Though El-Sayed declined to defend the Green New Deal in front of a national audience, he previously hasn’t been so shy.

A Fox News Digital review of El-Sayed's deleted social media posts, preserved via the Internet Archive, uncovered dozens of examples of the Michigan Senate hopeful defending the Green New Deal by name.

"Rather than announcing the next iteration of this or that car at [the North American International Auto Show 2019], I’d love to see automakers announce that they support the #GreenNewDeal," El-Sayed wrote in January of that year.

On the primary campaign trail, Rep. Haley Stevens criticized El-Sayed over his past support for the Green New Deal on the grounds that it could lead to job losses in the automobile manufacturing industry.
FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS: AS DEMOCRATS TURN LEFT, BLACK VOTERS TAP THE BRAKES
Abdul El-Sayed speaks to supporters at his Get Out to Vote rally in Detroit, Mich., on Aug. 3, 2026. (Jeff Kowalsky/AFP via Getty Images)
"The struggle for the Green New Deal uplifts the struggle for racial justice," El-Sayed wrote in April 2019.

The Green New Deal is a 2019 progressive policy framework floated by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Sen. Ed Markey, D-Mass., that seeks to gradually transition the United States’ electrical grid away from fossil fuels. Their plan has become synonymous with the left-wing faction of the Democratic Party, leading many Democrats running in competitive races to distance themselves from it.

In another post, from September 2019, El-Sayed wrote, "I believe in a Green New Deal" five times in all caps. He also suggested that the Green New Deal is essential to preserve freedom of speech because there can be no First Amendment "without the freedom to breathe the breath you have to take to speak in the first place."

"The #GreenNewDeal doesn’t center polar bears or glaciers, it centers those children forced to breath (sic.) in corporate pollution in their communities," El-Sayed wrote. "I stand with the Green New Deal because it stands for those kids."
WATCH: SURFACED VIDEOS OF DEM SENATE CANDIDATE BACKING 'DEFUND THE POLICE' CONTRADICT RECENT DENIALS
Abdul El-Sayed speaks before Sen. Bernie Sanders takes the stage at Mumford High School on May 3, 2026, in Detroit, Mich. (Getty Images)

CNN previously reported that El-Sayed scrubbed large swathes of his commentary from the internet prior to announcing his run for Senate. The deletions appear to have been selective, as he still has some posts up from before he launched his campaign.

In his since-deleted social media posts, El-Sayed endorsed the "defund the police" movement, argued cities spent too much policing poverty and described police departments as "standing armies we deploy against our own people." In a separate YouTube video that was later hidden, he floated replacing the Second Amendment’s right to bear arms with a constitutional right to healthcare and called Border Patrol agents "white supremacists" while blaming American policies for migration from struggling nations.
Though El-Sayed regularly mentioned the Green New Deal on X prior to running for Senate, he has not posted the phrase even once since announcing his candidacy, a review found.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

title: Texas law targeting drag shows could have criminalized the late Dolly Parton, judge ruled
summary: Judge David Hittner blocked Ken Paxton from enforcing Texas Senate Bill 12, citing First Amendment protections for drag shows and free speech.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A Texas law targeting drag show performances was struck down for the second time Tuesday by a Reagan-appointed judge who ruled that the law's "broad" language could even be applied to banning performances by Jennifer Lopez, Miley Cyrus and the now late Dolly Parton.
Gov. Greg Abbott signed Senate Bill 12 into law in June 2023, which prohibits "sexually oriented performances" from occurring in public places or where someone under 18-years-old may be present.
The law imposed up to a $10,000 fine on business owners for hosting drag show events. Performers at the events could have also been charged with a class A misdemeanor.

At the time, Abbott dubbed the law a ban on public drag performances on social media, prompting a lawsuit filed by LGBT organizations, entertainment groups and a drag queen performer. The lawsuit accused the law of being in violation of first speech rights.
IOWA TEACHERS SUSPENDED OVER VIRAL STUDENT-RUN DRAG SHOW REACH SETTLEMENT BEFORE TRIAL

A drag queen performs during a show at the Swan Dive nightclub on March 20, 2023, in Austin, Texas. Controversy and debate over four bills seeking to restrict drag shows in the state of Texas intensifies as lawmakers continue their proposals. Bills SB 8, SB 12, and SB1601 are scheduled for a hearing this Thursday. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

U.S. District Judge David Hittner ruled that the law can not stand because it is "unconstitutionally vague" and  "fails to give a reasonable person notice of what is prohibited," suggesting that any entertainers with sexual undertones in their performance could be penalized.

"Just as many people criticized Elvis’s signature hip gyrations and were offended by his display of male sexuality, chastised Dolly Parton as a voluptuous sex symbol because of her big hair, flamboyant clothes and breast exposure, and shamed Miley Cyrus for ‘twerking’ on stage during a live performance at the 2013 MTV Video Music Awards, there are ‘erotic’ elements in countless popular performances that could be subject to both civil and criminal penalties under S.B. 12," Hittner wrote.
GEORGIA PRIDE GROUP RECRUITING KIDS AS YOUNG AS 13 INTO DRAG SHOWS SPARKS BACKLASH

Hittner first struck down the law in September 2023 on five constitutional grounds, but while Texas’s appeal was pending, the Supreme Court issued its 2024 decision in Moody v. NetChoice, clarifying how courts must evaluate facial First Amendment challenges. The 5th Circuit Court of Appeals handed the case back down with further instructions on how to decide the case based on precedent set in the Moody decision.
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican candidate for the U.S. Senate, speaks during a primary election night watch party Tuesday, March 3, 2026, in Dallas. (Julio Cortez/AP Photo)
GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHER
Hittner again found the law unconstitutional, offering advice for those against drag shows.
"For those who find such activities as described in this case offensive, the solution is relatively simple ... just don't go," Hittner wrote in his briefing.

The Texas law sought to justify its ban on the claim that drag shows appeal to "the prurient interest," but Hittner brushed that claim aside, ruling that state law doesn't define what "prurient interest in sex" means.

"Because S.B. 12 does not specify who determines whether a performance ‘appeals to the prurient interest,’ or require that the work be taken as a whole, a single moment of eroticism could condemn an entire performance to criminal or civil penalties," Hittner wrote.

"There are ‘erotic’ elements in countless popular performances that could be subject to both civil and criminal penalties under S.B. 12," he wrote, going on to list "cheerleading, dancing, live theater, and other common public occurrences," as activities that could be banned under the law.
SEATTLE PRIDE PARADE PANDEMONIUM AS NUDE MARCHERS PRANCE THROUGH STREETS IN FRONT OF CHILDREN

Hittner immediately and permanently barred Attorney General Ken Paxton from enforcing the law and denied Paxton’s request for a new trial and additional discovery. However, Paxton, who is running for U.S. Senate, is able to appeal and said he intends to do so.

"This is a profoundly flawed decision that endangers our children and is an affront to Texas values," Paxton wrote on X. "I will appeal this decision immediately and continue to fight to protect our kids."
Fox News Digital reached to Paxton and Abbott's office for comment.
Drag performer Brigitte Bandit, a plantiff in the lawsuit, celebrated the ruling. Bandit's performances include impersonations of Dolly Parton, who passed away at 80-years old on Tuesday.

"Drag has always been a form of free expression, and it is a relief that the court recognized that today," Bandit said in a statement . "We use our performances to assert liberation, power, and joy with our community. As a lifelong Texan, I’m sick of this state trying to censor art and stoke hatred and violence against drag artists and the LGBTQIA+ community."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The ruling comes weeks after a federal appeals court approved a Florida law restricting children from sexually explicit performances, including many drag shows.

The Florida law defines an "adult live performance" as a live show that "depicts or simulates nudity, sexual conduct, sexual excitement, or specific sexual activities ... lewd conduct, or the lewd exposure of prosthetic or imitation genitals or breasts" and that also predominantly appeals to a "prurient, shameful, or morbid interest," is "patently offensive" for the age of the child present and, taken as a whole, lacks serious literary, artistic, political or scientific value for that child's age.
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: 'He's so thirsty': Newsom's 'enthusiastic' praise for Trump policy turns heads
summary: Gavin Newsom's public praise for Trump Accounts is raising 2028 presidential campaign speculation as observers question the California governor's motives.
story: ‘The Five’ co-hosts discuss California Gov. Gavin Newsom praising President Donald Trump’s Trump Accounts for children.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom's unusual public praise for President Donald Trump is raising political eyebrows, with observers suggesting the break from his usual posture could foreshadow how the Democrat positions himself ahead of 2028.

Newsom heaped praise on Trump accounts, or 530a accounts, which the president created with the help of Sens. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Cory Booker, D-N.J., to provide a market-indexed nest egg beginning at $1,000 for children born during his second term.

"Gavin Newsom, who fancies himself a 2028 nominee, has come out and said that he completely supports this and that he thinks it's the best thing President Trump has ever done," conservative writer Charles Hurt said in response.

"He is so thirsty," Hurt went on, adding on "Fox & Friends Weekend" that the remark reminded him of how some Democrats broke ranks to praise Trump’s "No Tax on Tips" plans that reduced federal levies on restaurant and service gratuities.
DEMOCRATIC MARYLAND GOV WES MOORE PRAISES TRUMP ACCOUNTS AS ‘SMART POLICY’
California Gov. Gavin Newsom and President Donald Trump. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images; Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images)
Former George W. Bush White House press secretary Dana Perino said on Fox News’ "The Five" that she believes Newsom's comments are indeed a "2028 play."

"I think this is going to pit some of the 20 candidates [against each other at debates if they are collectively asked] ‘Will you keep Trump accounts?’" she said. Perino suggested Newsom would have the upper hand and could point to his early support to counter allegations of political expediency.
California Assembly Minority Leader Alexandra Macedo told Fox News Digital that the rare collaboration on Trump accounts is encouraging but should be the rule, not the exception.
"It is good to see Gavin Newsom working with the Trump administration and recognizing a good idea when he sees one," said Macedo, R-Tulare.
"Hopefully this is not Halley’s Comet. Californians should not have to wait another 75 years for Newsom to do it again," she said.
During a news conference Friday, Newsom said Californians should consider opening a Trump account for their newborns, comparing the program to a Sacramento-based one championed by his wife.

"I’m enthusiastic about encouraging people to get a Trump account. I think it's incredibly important," Newsom said at an event alongside first lady Jennifer Siebel Newsom. "It's one of the best things he's done, and so we're here to encourage people to take advantage of this."
SEN DAVE MCCORMICK: TRUMP ACCOUNTS GIVE ALL AMERICANS A STAKE IN PROSPERITY
Gov. Gavin Newsom and President Donald Trump shake hands on Jan. 24, 2025, in Los Angeles, California. (Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images)
Newsom warned Californians not to "fall prey" to politics or cynicism, or "even the fear that if I download a Trump account somehow that means something."
"It doesn't, it just means something for your kid. It's not Trump's money. It's your child's money."
Siebel-Newsom spoke about a similar California program aimed at education expenses called "CalKIDS," which the Sacramento Bee reported has not had the same successful launch as Trump accounts.

Newsom recently called 2028 presidential conjecture "wildly premature," but acknowledged toying with the idea while taking steps that signal potential interest, including a nationally televised debate with potential Republican contender Gov. Ron DeSantis on Fox News Channel in 2023. He also told the Los Angeles Times more recently that "I’d be lying" if he said he hasn’t thought about running.
Fox News Digital reached out to Newsom for comment.
Some social media users also expressed surprise at Newsom’s tack.
JENNIFER SIEBEL NEWSOM DODGES QUESTION ON HUSBAND GAVIN'S PRESIDENTIAL ASPIRATIONS
"Uh oh... Newsom might have a decent campaign manager telling him to sound moderate, rational and team-building," one X user said.

"The outgoing Golden State governor and 2028 White House hopeful said that he is ‘enthusiastic’ about Trump accounts, the Republican leader’s initiative that created investment accounts for children under 18, with the federal government depositing $1,000 into accounts for babies born during the president’s second term," read a tweet from conservative podcaster Chad Law.
"Did something happen to Newsom?" added Defiant L’s, an account known for posting examples of liberals’ self-owns and perceived hypocrisies.

Fox News host Jesse Watters compared the effort to Bush’s much-maligned plan to privatize Social Security, calculating that returns for seniors would have doubled and the program would be solvent instead of facing potential insolvency in the 2030s.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Newsom also reiterated in a post on X that California was the "first state in the country" to make 5.5 million students eligible for the CalKIDS program for college and career expenses.

Newsom is one of several potential Democratic candidates representing different segments of the party, including socialist Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Biden administration Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Army vet lawmaker marks Abbey Gate anniversary with blistering message for Biden-Harris: 'Abject failure'
summary: Former Army aviator Rep. Matt Van Epps introduced a resolution marking five years since the deadly Abbey Gate bombing in Kabul, Afghanistan.
story: Rep. Matt Van Epps is introducing a resolution to mark five years since the bombing at Abbey Gate at the tail end of the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan.

FIRST ON FOX: Former Army aviator Rep. Matt Van Epps, R-Tenn., said he "vividly" remembers the moment five years ago when he heard the U.S. was withdrawing from Afghanistan with scant shreds of a plan in place.

"I remember my boss at the time in Tennessee state government asked me, like, 'Hey Matt, are you OK?' And, you know, I think the frank answer is no, I'm very upset about this," he told Fox News Digital in an interview. "And as I talked to my colleagues, some who were serving with me in government, others that were still active-duty Army and in the military, I think the feeling was generally the same, that we spent so much time and effort and to see that unfold the way that it did was just beyond frustrating."

To this day, Van Epps believes neither the Biden administration nor former President Joe Biden himself have been "adequately held responsible in the aftermath of just an absolutely chaotic withdrawal that did not have to happen."

It's part of what motivated him to introduce a resolution marking Wednesday's fifth anniversary of the tragic bombing at Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul, which took the lives of 13 U.S. service members in addition to over 100 Afghanis near the Abbey Gate.
GOLD STAR FATHER SAYS PRIOR AFGHANISTAN REVIEW SMELLED 'LIKE A COVER-UP' AS NEW LOOK EXAMINES MILLIONS OF DOCS

Afghanistan veteran and House lawmaker Rep. Matt Van Epps is marking five years since the bombing at Abbey Gate in Kabul, Afghanistan, with a blistering message for former President Joe Biden. (Drew Angerer/Getty Images; Marcus Yam/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)

"We've introduced this resolution, first and foremost, to remember that, coming up on five years ago, those 13 brave service members made the ultimate sacrifice at Abbey Gate," Van Epps said. "And then second to that is that the Biden-Harris administration absolutely failed to withdraw in Afghanistan, and it didn't have to be that way. And it's important for the American people to remember what the Biden-Harris administration did in that abject failure, withdrawing from Afghanistan."
AMERICA’S PROMISE TO OUR AFGHAN ALLIES IS STILL UNFINISHED FIVE YEARS LATER
Van Epps served 10 years of active duty that included deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan, spending part of that time as an air mission commander. He then served in the Tennessee Army National Guard.
And his ties to the withdrawal are personal, Van Epps said — two of his friends were on the ground in Kabul when the evacuation was taking place.
Rep. Matt Van Epps, R-Tenn., leaves the House Republican Conference caucus meeting at the Capitol Hill Club in Washington on May 13, 2026. (CQ-Roll Call, Inc. via Getty Images)

"I had two very close friends who were there as part of that evacuation. And they served honorably and heroically and did incredible work with the hand that they were dealt, they just should never have been put in that situation to begin with," he said.
The Biden administration faced bipartisan backlash for how it handled the withdrawal from Afghanistan amid the Taliban's lightning-fast takeover of the country.
TALIBAN WIPES OUT DECADES OF PROGRESS AS 2.4M AFGHAN GIRLS REMAIN LOCKED OUT OF SCHOOL, UN AGENCY SAYS

The majority of Democrats, however, have defended Biden. Many have said he was carrying out the work of President Donald Trump's agreement with the Taliban during his first administration in February 2020, which called for the U.S. to withdraw within 14 months.
DEMOCRATS CONDEMN DNC FOR POLITICIZING FALLEN SOLDIERS IN DELETED MEMORIAL DAY POST

Van Epps defended Trump's peace deal, arguing it cleared the way for a "very deliberate withdrawal from Afghanistan that had conditions that the Taliban and the Afghan government had to meet for us to withdraw our soldiers."

"And then the Biden team gets in, totally ignores the Doha agreement where they could have enforced those accountability measures on the Taliban, totally missed and ignored all of these warning signals as the Taliban was gaining ground across the country. They were more interested in optics than operations," he said.
Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.

title: SEE IT: LA Dem candidates torched by disgusted residents after ‘disgraceful’ debate: ‘Both bad’
summary: Los Angeles Democratic mayoral candidates Karen Bass and Nithya Raman face voter fury after a debate one resident called "disgraceful" for the city.
story: Los Angeles residents express their frustration with the remaining mayoral candidates as some express they believe they are "both bad."
Los Angeles’ Democratic mayoral candidates were torched by residents after a debate night in America’s second-most populous city that one voter described as "disgraceful."

Besides being home to Hollywood, Los Angeles is one of America’s most economically important cities. The city, however, has struggled with recent fires, rising living costs, homelessness and outmigration. Those problems have fueled a particularly contentious mayoral race this year, which included a surprisingly competitive but ultimately unsuccessful bid by Republican Spencer Pratt.

With Pratt out of the race, Democrats Karen Bass, the incumbent, and Nithya Raman, a democratic socialist city council member, are locked in a competitive and bitter runoff for Los Angeles mayor. During last week’s debate, Bass and Raman traded personal attacks and insults, leaving some voters frustrated over what solutions the candidates could offer.
After the debate, voter Stacey Segarra Bohlinger told Fox News Digital she believes Bass and Raman are "both bad" and said, "I wish they could both lose."

Mayor Karen Bass leaves a press conference as she visits the FEMA Disaster Recovery Center, following wildfires, in Los Angeles, Jan. 14, 2025. (Reuters/Daniel Cole)

Katchen reiterated that the two spoke as individuals and that their comments did not represent the Sherman Oaks Neighborhood Council. He called the debate a "success as determined by over 400 attendees, over 700 virtual viewers, NPR LAist live broadcast to what I was told over 500,000 listeners and covered by local, state, national and international media outlets." title: EXCLUSIVE: State Dept reveals Portland Antifa connection to Hamas, Iran’s IRGC in sweeping terror action
summary: A State Department memo reveals how an Italy-based tech collective built encrypted tools used by Antifa, Hamas and Hezbollah to organize attacks.
story: Journalist Andy Ngo and Frontlines TPUSA contributor Savanah Hernandez discuss their experiences reporting on rioters on 'The Ingraham Angle.'

EXCLUSIVE: A State Department memo reveals that an international technology collective, now under a U.S. global terrorism designation, provided services to overseas terrorist groups and violent far-left agitators causing chaos in American cities, according to a copy obtained by Fox News Digital.

"Far-left terrorism poses a profound threat to the United States and the broader West," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Today, the United States sanctioned Autistici/Inventati – a major far-left tech collective whose services are used by the most active and violent Antifa cells in the United States and across the world."

Autistici/Inventati, called the A/I Collective by the State Department, is an Italy-based group that builds highly sophisticated digital infrastructure used by violent left-wing organizations in the United States and Europe, along with Islamic terrorists, according to the State Department. The collective's services include encrypted chats and email, web hosting, secure video conferencing and streaming and anonymity shields, according to the memo.
'LEFT-WING EXTREMISTS,' CARTELS MOVE INTO CROSSHAIRS IN TRUMP TERROR SHIFT BEYOND ISIS
Demonstrators burn an American flag outside the ICE detention center in South Portland, Ore., on May 1, 2026. (Andrew Lichtenstein/Corbis via Getty Images)

"These tools are specifically designed to support the operations of far-left terrorist networks, built to enable them to organize, recruit, communicate, disseminate propaganda, share target information and tactics, and carry out violent attacks – all while remaining anonymous, untraceable, and beyond the reach of the law," says the State Department's memo.

A/I Collective has officially been deemed a Specially Designated Global Terrorist. The designation bars Americans and U.S. financial institutions from doing business with the group and freezes any assets it has under U.S. jurisdiction. Violators can face civil or criminal penalties.
The memo identifies Portland-based Rose City Antifa, known for its violent rioting and destruction, as one of the U.S. groups that relied on A/I Collective tools and services.
FORMER MARINE GETS 100 YEARS IN PRISON AS JUDGE CALLS ICE DETENTION CENTER AMBUSH 'AN ASSAULT ON DEMOCRACY'

Rose City Antifa is listed in the memo alongside a media organization that the State Department says uses A/I Collective tools to disseminate information to the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), which is proliferating inside the United States, Hamas, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Hezbollah and others.
President Donald Trump designated Antifa a domestic terrorist organization via a September 2025 executive order. (Diego Diaz/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

The memo also accuses the militant abortion-rights group "Jane’s Revenge" — which declared "open season" on pro-life organizations and threatened escalating attacks after the leaked Supreme Court draft signaling Roe v. Wade would be overturned — of using the collective’s services.
The State Department memo says the collective provides its services exclusively to left-wing extremists, screening users for ideological alignment before allowing them access to its tools.

The collective claims to host roughly 16,000 mailboxes, 1,500 websites, 5,500 mailing lists and 10,000 "blogs" on a custom-built platform. The State Department says militants frequently use those services to disseminate target information, tactical manuals and techniques and communiqués about recent attacks.
RUBIO'S CALL TO COMBAT GLOBAL FUNDERS OF FAR-LEFT TERRORISM COULD PUT SINGHAM IN CROSSHAIRS

The memo stressed that while the infrastructure is overseas, it supports domestic far-left groups that for years have wreaked havoc in the United States, mostly under the label of Antifa, or antifascism.

Hamas fighters secure an area before handing over Israeli-American hostage Keith Siegel to a Red Cross team in Gaza City on Feb. 1, 2025, as part of the fourth hostage-prisoner exchange. (OMAR AL-QATTAA/AFP via Getty Images)
TRUMP’S COUNTERTERRORISM STRATEGY SCORES BIG WINS AGAINST GLOBAL TERROR THREATS

"There will be no refuge for violent extremists who wage war on our civilization and plot to undermine law and order, destroy critical infrastructure, assault political opponents, or conspire to conceal their crimes from authorities," Rubio said. "We will use all the tools and authorities at our disposal to fight terrorism and protect our way of life from terrorist coercion."
The memo cites several examples of violent or terrorist activity that the State Department says was facilitated through A/I Collective technology.
SECRET SIGNAL CHATS REVEAL HOW ANTI-ICE AGITATORS COORDINATED NEWARK RIOTS

The memo identifies a far-left extremist media group that describes itself as a "tool" for militants worldwide to share "essential information" to be "acted upon." According to State, the group relies on A/I Collective services to publish official communiqués and calls to action for U.S.-designated foreign terrorist organizations.

The memo says Rose City Antifa relied on A/I Collective tools and services to organize and incite violent and criminal acts, including disseminating an online flyer urging supporters to use laser pointers against U.S. Customs and Border Protection helicopters.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David, the presidential retreat, on July 31, 2026, in Camp David, Md. Trump convened members of his Cabinet at the retreat as the war with Iran continues. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)
ANTI-ICE AGITATORS THROW WOODEN PALLETS, MATTRESSES AT FEDERAL AGENTS DURING CHAOTIC NJ DETENTION CENTER CLASH

"All you need is a laser. Leave home – they can see where the laser is coming from," the flyer said. "Go to a park, a field, or some other public place, and once the clock strikes 9 unleash your beam at the cop copter. Mask up. Coordinate with friends to throw a laser party!"
"Let’s take back the night together!" it continued. "It won’t take many of us to ground the helicopters!"
The memo says at least one man answered the call to action. Federal records show he later pleaded guilty to aiming a laser at a CBP helicopter, forcing the aircraft to abort its planned landing.

The memo says Rose City Antifa also used A/I Collective tools to disseminate personal information about U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement personnel and calls for targeted attacks against ICE agents "in their homes" and in public.
People attend a vigil and protest outside of Columbia University on October 7, 2025, in New York City. (Adam Gray/Getty Images)

"Jane's Revenge" used A/I Collective tools to "publish official communiqués and claims of responsibility for violent and criminal acts and to incite copycat attacks," according to the State Department.

Notably, Jane’s Revenge claimed responsibility for the May 2022 firebombing of a crisis pregnancy center in Madison, Wisconsin. The following day, a cryptic message appeared on a blog affiliated with the group.
THREE ALLEGED ANTIFA-LINKED PROTESTERS INDICTED IN ATLANTA POLICE TRAINING CENTER CONTRACTOR FIREBOMBING

"This was only a warning. We demand the disbanding of all anti-choice establishments, fake clinics, and violent anti-choice groups within the next thirty days," the message said. "This is not a mere 'difference of opinion' as some have framed it. We are literally fighting for our lives. We will not sit still while we are killed and forced into servitude. We have run thin on patience and mercy for those who seek to strip us of what little autonomy we have left."

At approximately 2:30 a.m., on June 10, 2022, Gresham Police responded to an alarm at the Gresham Pregnancy Resource Center located at 104 NW 11th Street. Once on scene, law enforcement personnel found a fire inside the building. Investigators believe several Molotov cocktails were thrown through a kitchen window in order to ignite the fire. Investigators found several large bottles in the kitchen with fire accelerant confirmed on the floor. (FBI Portland)

In the following months, several more posts appeared claiming responsibility for vandalism of pregnancy centers across the country, including smashed glass windows and doors and graffiti. The State Department memo says that four members of the group were later federally charged for "'conspiracy against rights' through threats of force and intimidation."
The memo also refers to far-left extremists in Atlanta using A/I Collective tools and services in a violent attempt to "prevent the construction of a law enforcement training center."
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also weighed in.

"Far-left extremists, their fronts, and their enablers should be on notice: We will bring the full weight of our economic tools to bear," he said. "Political terrorism has no place in our society, and we will continue to cut the financial lifelines of these groups until they are eliminated."
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks at a news conference, Monday, Aug. 24, 2026, at the Treasury Department in Washington. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson)

Abroad, the memo says far-left extremists in France, Italy, Germany and the Netherlands used A/I Collective tools to claim responsibility for attacks on rail systems this year and to disseminate instructions for making improvised incendiary devices intended to disrupt railways.

Anarchists who claimed responsibility for sabotaging infrastructure supporting the Transalpine Pipeline, a major crude-oil artery into Central Europe, also used A/I Collective tools, according to the memo. The State Department says the same was true of the far-left Vulkangruppe, which has targeted German infrastructure since 2011 and claimed responsibility for a January attack that knocked out power to roughly 45,000 Berlin households.
